messages:
maria: Running a full nsys run on the weird perf regression we saw on prod-like load. Uploading trace: https://perf.company/traces/1806501234
aj: which nsys + driver + kernel?
maria: nsys 2024.2.1, CUDA 12.2, driver 535.54.03, kernel 5.15.0-70-generic
aj: container cfg? privileged? mounts?
maria: container had /dev/nvidia0 /dev/nvidiactl mounted but not privileged or CAP_SYS_ADMIN. nsight attach failed initially with permission errors.
sam: saw that too. stderr had CUPTI errors then an ioctl EPERM from nsys when trying to enable CUPTI activities.
maria: exact snippet: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] ERROR: CUPTI: cuptiActivityEnable returned CUPTI_ERROR_INTERNAL
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] ERROR: nsys attaching failed: ioctl(NVDRV_IOCTL_GPU_CTRL) = -1 EPERM
```
aj: if you rerun privileged does it attach cleanly?
maria: yes, with --cap-add SYS_ADMIN the attach proceeds, but the resulting timeline shows a bunch of short kernels separated by scheduling gaps. Perf regressions persist even when attach succeeds.
sam: timeline screenshot: attention kernel launches are ~120us but there are 30–60us gaps between them. That increases end-to-end token latency by ~18%.
maria: hypothesis: batching heuristic decider flips to per-request KV cache hot path when avg seq len drops. That path ends up doing a CPU-bound kv lookup with a lock which yields and forces the GPU stream to idle.
aj: can you paste the host perf stat / perf top around the gaps?
maria: grabbed perf samples, top shows heavy contention on 'kv_store::get_locked' and 'epoll_wait' during those windows. Also see recurring schedule events where thread gets preempted.
sam: could be two things: (1) the CUPTI/driver attach changes scheduler affinities or introduces extra synchronization; (2) our kernel selection logic is emitting small kernels when KV cache hits reduce compute per step.
perf-bot: auto-note: comparing traces: baseline trace (no CUPTI attach) vs attached trace shows additional 3–4ms total overhead per batch due to host-side syscall spikes.
maria: repro steps I used:
```
# run in container (non-privileged, reproduces EPERM)
docker run --gpus all -v /dev:/dev --rm my/runtime-image:latest /bin/bash -c "python -m myapp.bench --profile nsys"
# run in privileged to get attach and weird gaps
docker run --gpus all --cap-add SYS_ADMIN -v /dev:/dev --rm my/runtime-image:latest /bin/bash -c "nsys profile -o out ./run_bench.sh"
```
aj: can you try nsys with --sample=kernel and with CUPTI disabled to compare? also try nvidia-smi -q to ensure driver isn't in a degraded state.
maria: did a quick compare: disabling CUPTI (nsys --sample=none) reduces host syscall spikes but still leaves the batching fragmentation when kv cache hits rate > 60%. So two contributors.
sam: on the kernel-selection side: our heuristic uses measured avg tokens-per-batch to pick kernel tile sizes. If KV hits short-circuit the forward path we under-estimate work and pick narrow tiles, causing many kernel launches. Suggest: add a secondary rule to prefer coarser tiles when KV-hit ratio high to keep GPU busy.
aj: agree. Also file a bug with NVIDIA about the attach EPERM in non-priv containers — that breaks observability in our Dedicated offering unless we document the capability requirement. Might be a driver security change.
maria: opened internal ticket PERF-1942 with logs, nsys output, and minimal repro. added driver version and kernel info.
deploy-bot: NOTE: PERF-1942 created by maria at 2026-03-10T14:21:00Z
sam: short-term mitigation: tweak batch heuristic to avoid switching to micro-batches when KV-hit ratio > 40% and enforce a minimal kernel coalescing time window (e.g., 500us) to let adjacent launches merge. I'll draft a patch.
aj: also add a metric for host-side preemptions in Console (schedule_yields per route) so we can detect this automatically.
maria: next actions: (1) sam to prototype heuristic patch, (2) aj to add schedule_yields metric, (3) I will continue digging on CUPTI attach repro and open with NVIDIA if EPERM persists.
aj: thanks! if you need me to escalate vendor support ping me. :thumbsup:
